items.title: Browser Use in Managed Deep Agents
items.en_title: Browser Use in Managed Deep Agents
items.en_oneliner: The managed version of Deep Agents now handles browsing for your agent, tuning its tools to save context, and hands the login step back to you.

items.title: How We Optimized Browser Use for Deep Agents
items.en_title: How We Optimized Browser Use for Deep Agents
items.en_oneliner: The post walks through how the team tested seven browser toolsets, chose Browserbase's Stagehand, and refined it using LangSmith traces and evals.

items.title: Agents Are Going Async
items.en_oneliner: Because async subagents keep the main agent responsive while long tasks run in the background, this post walks through the orchestration, notifications, and approvals that make it work.

items.title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
items.en_title: Partnering with Hacktron to find vulnerabilities in OpenAI’s systems
items.en_oneliner: OpenAI has teamed up with Hacktron to hunt for vulnerabilities and test third-party service connections, using frontier AI to shore up its own defenses.

items.title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
items.en_title: Measuring how AI agents handle everyday wet-lab science
items.en_oneliner: OpenAI's new BioBasicsBench runs agents through 100 tasks to gauge how they interpret raw lab data and tackle routine wet-lab work.

items.title: Spaces
items.en_oneliner: Amp launches Spaces, a new way to work with agents and your team, where one agent spawns and coordinates others on your behalf.

items.title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
items.en_title: Egyptian and Nigerian English join the Open ASR Leaderboard
items.en_oneliner: The Open ASR Leaderboard now covers Egyptian and Nigerian English, widening the evaluation of speech recognition across accents.

items.title: Close the Loop
items.en_oneliner: Amp adds a feedback widget for websites, letting visitors send feedback straight to the team by visiting the site with ?amp appended.

items.title: Cult.fit builds operational muscle with Codex
items.en_title: Cult.fit builds operational muscle with Codex
items.en_oneliner: At Cult.fit, teams across functions are building tools with Codex and moving faster, changing how day-to-day work gets done.

items.title: Introducing bots in Kiro Crew
items.en_oneliner: Kiro Crew adds bots that run several agent sessions at once — one refactoring your auth module, another chasing a flaky test, a third drafting a database migration plan.

items.title: process-daemon v0.5.0
items.en_oneliner: The terminal component opencode-pty reaches 0.5.0 on protocol 8, now published to npm.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.en_title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.en_oneliner: The new multimodal model is built for speed and low cost, and it handles longer audio and video clips for budget-sensitive use cases.

items.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.en_title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast and cost-effective with longer clips
items.en_oneliner: Google introduces Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, a fast, low-cost multimodal model that supports longer clips.

items.title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates
items.en_title: Australian universities are creating AI-native graduates
items.en_oneliner: Universities across Australia are widening access to ChatGPT and weaving AI into teaching, so students graduate ready for an AI-shaped workplace.

items.title: Devin Review 2.0
items.en_oneliner: Devin Review 2.0 now reviews pull requests at 82% lower cost than before, so teams can afford to run it on every PR.
